slides.sub: The Prodigy. Essex, 1990. A raver who became the face of a generation.

text: Liam Howlett handed him a tape.
He came back the next day.
Let me dance to your music.
slides.sub: A dancer found a producer. Neither knew what it would become.
Music for the Jilted Generation was written in that anger.
The dancer became the frontman. The face rave never had.
A warehouse dancer's band had just conquered the world.

slides.note: Maxim. Keith Flint. Liam Howlett. Three roles, one explosion. Genre stopped meaning anything.

slides.sub: A mural went up in Hackney. Near the club where he first took the stage in 1990.

slides.strobe: It started with one man dancing in a warehouse. That was the whole story.
